quarterly_data.signal: At its 2026 Investor Day Synopsys gave full fiscal year 2027 targets (fiscal year ending October 31, 2027): revenue $11,100 million to $11,200 million, which the company describes as revenue growth of approximately 15% year over year to $11.15 billion at the midpoint of the guidance range; GAAP operating margin ~20.7% and non-GAAP operating margin ~44.0% at the midpoint; GAAP EPS $8.16 to $8.61 and non-GAAP EPS $19.04 to $19.12; non-GAAP tax rate 18%; operating cash flow ~$3,600 million, free cash flow ~$3,100 million and capital expenditures ~$500 million.

quarterly_data.quarter: Synopsys press release: Synopsys Details Growth Strategy and Long-term Financial (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Updated long-term objectives for FY26E-FY30E (provided as of September 30, 2026; growth figures are FY26E-FY30E CAGRs): company revenue mid-teens growth, ~15%; Design Automation - EDA mid-teens 13%+ and simulation and analysis (S&A) double-digit 10%+; Design IP high-teens 17%+; FY30E non-GAAP operating margin ~50%; free cash flow growth in the mid 20%s; non-GAAP EPS growth in the mid 20%s. CEO Sassine Ghazi: 'AI is creating multiple, reinforcing growth engines for Synopsys' - frontier intelligence is fueling 'an unprecedented demand for compute power while increasing system complexity', purpose-built silicon is reshaping the IP market, and Physical AI and agentic workflows are driving deeper integration of its tools, expanding the addressable market and creating new, recurring revenue streams. The company says it will monetize AI-driven engineering through a combination of subscription and consumption-based models across tools, agents and platform.
quarterly_data.figure: FY26E-FY30E revenue CAGR ~15% (EDA 13%+, S&A 10%+, Design IP 17%+); FY30E non-GAAP operating margin ~50%; FCF and non-GAAP EPS growth in the mid 20%s

quarterly_data.quarter: Synopsys press release: Synopsys Details Growth Strategy and Long-term Financial (09-30-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Investor Day: Synopsys is expanding its silicon IP business beyond traditional standards-based IP into application-optimized IP (AOIP) - optimized IP subsystems and platforms for differentiated custom silicon, as AI drives custom-silicon demand across hyperscalers and system companies. The company says this 'Factory 2' IP model expands its value capture per design win and its participation in the growth of custom silicon and AI infrastructure. It has secured multiple AOIP customers spanning compute, ASIC and AI connectivity architectures, including the IP agreement with Amazon announced the same day (other customers not named).
